newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims rise in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims rise in latest week.

text.p: The number of people filing new claims for unemployment benefits in late October rose by 23,000, the government said on Thursday.
The Labour Department said 342,000 people filed first-time claims for unemployment insurance benefits in the week ended Oct. 26, up from 319,000 claims in the previous week.

The rise brought the average weekly rate of new claims over the past four weeks -- a more accurate measurement of employment trends than the more-volatile weekly numbers -- to 331,250, up from 331,000 in the prior four-week period.

Total benefit rolls rose 23,000 to reach 2.450 million in the week ended Oct. 19, the latest period for which those figures were available. That was up from 2.427 million the prior week, the department said.
It said Michigan and Mississippi reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Oct. 19, the latest period for which those data are available.
Michigan, with 2,150 additional claims, cited layoffs in the automobile industry, an indirect effect of the General Motors Corp. strike in Canada.
Mississippi reported 1,458,layoffs, mostly in the apparel, industrial machinery, computer, electrical and transportation equipment industries, and in manufacturing.
The Labour Department said eight states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Oct. 19 week.
Among the largest were California, with 5,301 fewer initial claims, Pennsylvania with 4,592, Ohio with 4,046 and Missouri with 2,758.
California cited fewer layoffs in all industries. Pennsylvania had fewer layoffs in the food, service and transportation equipment industries.
Missouri reported fewer layoffs in the construction, trade, service and transportation industries. Ohio had no comment.
